name: Jupiter
hook: The biggest planet, its four famous moons, and the god Jeopardy keeps asking about.

facts.label: the king of the Roman gods
facts.statement: Jupiter is named for the supreme Roman god, son of Saturn and husband of Juno; the Greeks called him Zeus.

facts.label: the Great Red Spot
facts.statement: The Great Red Spot is Jupiter's giant storm; Robert Hooke spotted it in 1664, and Pioneer 10 images showed hurricane-like winds cause it.

facts.label: the Galilean moons
facts.statement: In 1610 Galileo discovered Jupiter's four largest moons and called them the Medicean stars; two-letter Io has volcanic regions hotter than Mercury's surface.

facts.label: Ganymede
facts.statement: Ganymede is the largest moon of Jupiter and of the solar system, and the only moon known to have its own magnetic field.

facts.label: Pioneer 10
facts.statement: Pioneer 10, launched in 1972, was the first spacecraft sent to Jupiter and is now more than 6 billion miles from Earth.

facts.label: the asteroid belt
facts.statement: The asteroid belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter; Ceres, the first asteroid found there, was discovered in 1801.

facts.label: jovial
facts.statement: The word "jovial" comes from the Latin for "under the influence of Jupiter" — those born under his sign were thought joyful.
